prompt.title: Hexagonal vertical slice scaffolder

variables.var: the same package as a source path

var.name: spec_excerpt
var.example: SPEC.md 3.2 PlaceOrder: POST /orders with Idempotency-Key; NEW to RESERVED on stock reserved; emits OrderPlaced; INV-3 amount positive.

variables.var: the SPEC.md section for this slice, verbatim
current layout, so new code lands where it belongs

var.name: existing_conventions
var.example: Records, no Lombok; constructor injection; problem+json errors; Spotless palantir format.

variables.var: the parts of CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules that apply

context.platform: Java 21 source level on a JDK 25 runtime; Spring Boot 4.1.2 with its managed versions (Spring Framework 7, HikariCP 7.0.2, jOOQ 3.21.9, Flyway 12.4.0, Testcontainers 2.0.5, JUnit 6.0.3); Resilience4j 2.4.0 (resilience4j-spring-boot4); OpenTelemetry Spring Boot starter 2.33.1.

instructions.step: Restate the slice contract from the spec in at most ten lines: inputs, outputs, state change, events, errors, idempotency. If the spec is silent on any of these, stop and ask.
Write the domain first: records and sealed result types in {{base_package}}.domain, with the invariants as constructor or method checks and unit tests beside them. No framework imports.
Write the application layer: the {{slice}} use case in {{base_package}}.application, an inbound port it implements, and the outbound ports it needs. The use case owns the transaction boundary.

Write the adapters: a REST controller that maps to problem details and honours Idempotency-Key; a {{persistence}} repository implementing the persistence port; an outbox writer for the domain events; each outbound HTTP client wrapped in a Resilience4j time limiter and circuit breaker.

Write the next Flyway migration (never edit an applied one) and the configuration: virtual threads on, an explicit Hikari pool size with the sizing arithmetic in a comment, OpenTelemetry resource attributes.
Write the tests: domain unit tests, a web slice test, a Testcontainers PostgreSQL integration test using @ServiceConnection, and an ArchUnit test for the layer rules.
Run the verification commands, fix until they pass, and report.

invariants.inv: Domain classes import nothing from org.springframework, jakarta.persistence, org.jooq or the adapter packages.
@Transactional appears only on application-layer public methods called from outside the bean; no self-invocation, no transactions in controllers.
Every outbound port has exactly one production adapter and one in-memory test double.

The Hikari maximum pool size is set explicitly; with virtual threads the pool, not the thread count, limits database concurrency, so pool size times replica count stays below the database's connection budget.
Every outbound network call has a timeout and a circuit breaker; retries only on idempotent calls.
Domain events are written to the outbox in the same transaction as the state change, with the W3C traceparent in the event headers.
A repeated POST with the same Idempotency-Key returns the original result and changes nothing.

anti_goals.no: No Lombok, field injection or service locators.
No H2 or embedded databases in persistence tests.
No new dependency beyond the platform list without asking first.
No catch-all exception handlers that log and continue.
No synchronized blocks around blocking I/O (on a JDK 21 runtime they pin virtual threads); use ReentrantLock.

output_contract.file: aggregate, value objects, domain events, sealed results
domain tests, web slice test, Testcontainers IT, ArchitectureTest
output_contract.report: The commands you ran with their pass/fail summary lines, each invariant with the file and test that enforces it, and any deviation from the spec with the reason.

verification.check: ArchitectureTest: domain must not depend on Spring, JPA, jOOQ or adapter packages.
ArchitectureTest: @Transactional methods live only in application classes; grep shows no this-calls to them.
List each outbound port with its adapter and its test double.
Quote the pool-size line and its arithmetic.
List each outbound client with its Resilience4j instance names and timeouts.
The Testcontainers IT asserts the outbox row and its traceparent exist after the use case commits, and none after a rollback.
The web or integration test sends the same POST twice and asserts one state change and identical responses.

prompt.task: Implement the {{slice}} vertical slice end to end as specified, satisfying every invariant, then report against the output contract.
